name: Do you have a documented approach on how to classify, prioritise and redress vulnerabilities?
conditionsText: Different vulnerabilities may require different responses. The guidance gives examples including patches or updates, compensating controls, code fixes and workarounds, with more serious issues potentially requiring senior-management escalation
requirementTitle: Do you have a documented approach on how to classify, prioritise and redress vulnerabilities?
requirementDescription: Have you agreed and written down how you will judge how serious a vulnerability is, decide which ones need fixing first, and determine how and when they will be fixed?
why:
Not every vulnerability presents the same level of risk. A minor weakness in a low-risk component should not necessarily receive the same priority as a critical vulnerability affecting an important internet-facing system.
Having an agreed process ensures vulnerabilities are handled consistently and that teams focus first on weaknesses presenting the greatest risk.
tasks: Do you have a documented approach on how to classify, prioritise and redress vulnerabilities?

actions.title: Do you have a documented approach on how to classify, prioritise and redress vulnerabilities?
actions.description:
Create and maintain a documented vulnerability management process that defines:
• how vulnerabilities are classified and scored
• how priority is determined
• expected remediation timescales
• available remediation approaches
• who is responsible for resolving them
• when vulnerabilities need escalating
• how remediation is tested and confirmed
• how vulnerabilities are recorded and tracked.
